extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is introduced as the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding. It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with 4,750 test instances, and all datasets are standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of large language models.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai; Xin Lv; Jiajie Zhang; Hongchang Lyu; Jiankai Tang; Zhidian Huang; Zhengxiao Du; Xiao Liu; Aohan Zeng; Lei Hou; Yuxiao Dong; Jie Tang; Juanzi Li
extraction.citeAs: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, and Juanzi Li. 2024. LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench was assembled from 21 datasets across 6 task categories: 6 datasets were directly extracted from original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 were built based on original datasets and processed for long-context evaluation, and 5 were created by the authors. Public datasets were extracted mainly from their test sets to avoid test leakage, except VCSUM. For MultiFieldQA, the authors first collected documents and articles from multiple sources and then manually curated the dataset. For multi-document QA, English test samples were built from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue, and a Chinese dataset was constructed based on DuReader. For synthetic tasks, PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh were constructed from English Wikipedia and the Chinese sections of the C4 dataset, and PassageCount was built by randomly selecting passages from English Wikipedia. The LCC dataset was sampled from the original Long Code Completion dataset, and RepoBench-P was adapted from GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors extracted data from the test sets of collected public datasets, with the exception of VCSUM due to its insufficient data in its test set.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data include original public datasets and source corpora such as NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, the Long Code Completion dataset, RepoBench-P, English Wikipedia, the Chinese sections of the C4 dataset, and documents collected for MultiFieldQA from legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers, Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and Chinese Government Website.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA in English and Chinese, the authors manually curated documents from multiple sources and invited three Ph.D. students to annotate one question and one ground-truth answer for each article; guidelines required clear questions with definitive and relatively short answers, random distribution of evidence paragraphs throughout the article, varied question types, and ensuring answers could be inferred from the documents. The annotators were expert NLP Ph.D. students, and cross-validation among annotators was performed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators shows a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Ph.D. students; extensive research experience in NLP; expert annotators
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The placement of evidence is fairly random to avoid biases that might occur if, for instance, the answer-related statements are frequently found at the beginning or the end
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect the quality of the response and may underestimate models that generate longer responses; performance on LongBench is coupled with the models’ instruction-following capabilities
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluating long context understanding; gauging long context understanding abilities of LLMs; measuring how model performance changes under different context lengths within the same task; serving as testbeds for future research in long context modeling
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All 21 datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, among which 6 are directly extracted from the original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on the original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by us. To tailor the data for long-context evaluation, we utilize complete Wikipedia passages encompassing the supporting or distracting paragraphs as the context. Initially, supporting passages are included within the context, and then as many distracting passages are added until the total length reaches a maximum length. Finally, these passages are randomly ordered to form the multi-document context. To adapt [DuReader] for assessing long context ability, for each question, we not only provide several documents related to the question but also arbitrarily select several from the total set of documents as distractors, until each question is associated with 20 documents. In each of the above datasets adapted for LongBench, for each test data, we first randomly select an integer within a range as the number of examples, then randomly sample the corresponding number of samples from the training set, and concatenate them to form the context C. For each data entry, we randomly sample 30 passages and select one of them for summarization using GPT-3.5-Turbo. For each piece of data, we randomly select several passages from English Wikipedia, repeat each paragraph at random several times, and finally shuffle the paragraphs. For each original piece of data, we shuffle the cross-file code snippets that include the gold cross-file code snippet, and combine them into context C. We employ two extraction strategies: random sampling and uniform sampling.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format. We filter the passages in TriviaQA with less than 1,000 words to be examples. In LongBench, we include “Document i” before the ith news article, and concatenate them into the context C. In LongBench, we select the long segments from VCSUM to compose our evaluation samples. Since LLMs may have already been trained on the training set of some of our collected public datasets, to avoid test leakage, we extract data from the test sets of these public datasets, with the exception of VCSUM due to its insufficient data in its test set.
